findings.evidence: DOM order is #s3-step3 "Confirm your order" (style="order:3"), then #s3-step2 "Enter payment details" (style="order:2"), then #s3-step1 "Choose a plan" (style="order:1").
findings.fix: Reorder the step <div> elements in the DOM itself to match the intended reading sequence (Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order) instead of relying on CSS order to resequence them only visually.
findings.violation: The CSS order property resequences the three steps for sighted display into Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order, while the underlying DOM order presents them in the reverse sequence, so a linearized reading reaches the confirmation step before hearing what is being chosen or paid for.

findings.evidence: The only navigation mechanisms on the page are the header nav ("Plan a trip", "Service alerts") and the footer links ("Privacy policy", "Terms of service"); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere in the document.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent wayfinding mechanism, such as a site search form or a breadcrumb trail reflecting this page's place in the site.
findings.violation: Fewer than two independent mechanisms exist to locate this page ("Rider service updates") within the site, and the page's own content does not mark it as one step in a linear process that would exempt it.

findings.fix: Use a native <button> element, or add role="button", an accessible name such as aria-label="Delete", and keyboard support (tabindex="0" with Enter/Space handling).
findings.violation: The div exposes no role, no programmatically determinable accessible name, and no keyboard affordance; its only content is an icon marked alt="" (decorative), so nothing identifies this control's existence or purpose to assistive technology.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>, with no asterisk, no "required" text, and no other field in the form styled this way.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal alongside the styling, such as a "required" suffix or an icon with its own text alternative, or remove the color if no distinction from the other labels is intended.
findings.violation: The red color is the only signal distinguishing the "Phone number" label from the form's other labels (Route, Email address, Promo code), with no accompanying text, icon, or other non-color signal carrying the same meaning.

findings.evidence: Heading "Accessibility improvements" is followed by #s1-p1 (requesting a fare adjustment through the mobile app or in person) and #s1-p2 (checking real-time arrivals by phone), neither of which concerns disability accessibility.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to match its actual content, e.g. "Fare adjustments and arrival information," or move genuinely accessibility-related content under it.
findings.violation: The heading's wording does not describe the topic of the content that actually follows it, so a reader scanning headings for accessibility-related changes is misled about what this section covers.

findings.evidence: Heading "Weekend service" is immediately followed by #s2-p1, "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person," with no weekend-specific content before the table.
findings.fix: Move the fare-adjustment paragraph to the section it actually belongs to, or rewrite it to address weekend service specifically.
findings.violation: The heading's wording does not describe the paragraph that immediately follows it, so a reader scanning headings for weekend-service information is misled about what the section covers.

findings.evidence: Error., associated with .
findings.fix: Replace the message with specific text naming the problem, e.g. "Promo code not recognized. Check for typos and try again."
findings.violation: The error text is the generic placeholder "Error." and states neither which rule the promo-code value failed nor what to change, leaving the reader only able to infer which field is at fault from its position in the markup.
